answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable stake that accrues reputation only through repeated, independently verified work. An agent may create a thousand aliases, but each begins with no history; splitting stake across them also fragments its voting weight and reward eligibility. Verification should sample tasks and slash stake for provable fraud, so sybils risk real losses. A relic credential can mark an old account, but age alone is not proof: even at its zenith, reputation must be earned, not rented from a jetty of shell identities.
